routeparity audit  ingress class "nginx"
  6 Ingresses · 5 hosts · 6 paths
  converter warnings from github.com/kubernetes-sigs/ingress2gateway@v1.2.0 (standard emitter)
  note: 6 of 6 Ingresses have no creationTimestamp. ingress-nginx resolves conflicting rules in
  favour of the oldest Ingress, so precedence between them is assumed, not known. Export manifests
  from the cluster to keep timestamps.

HIGH    NGX-CONVERT-001  The converter did not translate a feature
        Ingress/demo/admin
        ingress2gateway: Unsupported annotation nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-url
        because: this controls who can reach the backend; without it requests that were rejected are
        served

HIGH    NGX-REGEX-002  Regex mode applies to every path on the host
        regex-match.example.com /Header  ·  Ingress/demo/regex-match-other
        Exact path "/Header" is matched as a case-insensitive regex prefix, because another Ingress
        on this host enables regex mode. Translated literally it will stop matching requests that
        differ in case or have a longer path.
        because: Ingress/demo/regex-match sets use-regex
        fix: Match the path as a case-insensitive regular expression that also accepts longer paths.
        RegularExpression support and syntax are implementation-specific, so confirm your Gateway
        accepts the (?i) flag.
            matches:
            - path:
                type: RegularExpression
                value: "(?i)/Header.*"

HIGH    NGX-REGEX-001  Regex paths match case-insensitively and as a prefix
        regex-match.example.com /[A-Z]{3}  ·  Ingress/demo/regex-match
        ingress-nginx matches "/[A-Z]{3}" as a case-insensitive regular expression anchored only at
        the start. A RegularExpression match with the same value matches fewer requests on gateways
        that match the whole path case-sensitively.
        fix: Match the path as a case-insensitive regular expression that also accepts longer paths.
        RegularExpression support and syntax are implementation-specific, so confirm your Gateway
        accepts the (?i) flag.
            matches:
            - path:
                type: RegularExpression
                value: "(?i)/[A-Z]{3}.*"

HIGH    NGX-REGEX-003  rewrite-target turns on regex matching
        rewrite-target.example.com /IP  ·  Ingress/demo/rewrite-target
        Exact path "/IP" is matched as a case-insensitive regex prefix because its Ingress sets
        rewrite-target ("/uuid"). A URLRewrite filter on a literal Exact or PathPrefix match will
        rewrite fewer requests.
        fix: Match the path as a case-insensitive regular expression that also accepts longer paths.
        RegularExpression support and syntax are implementation-specific, so confirm your Gateway
        accepts the (?i) flag.
            matches:
            - path:
                type: RegularExpression
                value: "(?i)/IP.*"

MEDIUM  NGX-TLS-001  Hosts with TLS redirect HTTP to HTTPS
        path-normalization.example.com
        ingress-nginx answers plain HTTP requests for 1 path(s) on this host with a 308 redirect to
        HTTPS. The Gateway needs an HTTP listener with a redirecting HTTPRoute to do the same.
        fix: Attach a redirect-only HTTPRoute to the HTTP listener for this host.
            rules:
            - filters:
              - type: RequestRedirect
                requestRedirect:
                  scheme: https
                  statusCode: 308

MEDIUM  NGX-SLASH-001  A path ending in a slash redirects the slashless request
        trailing-slash.example.com /my-path/  ·  Ingress/demo/trailing-slash
        ingress-nginx answers "/my-path" with a 301 redirect to "/my-path/". Without an explicit
        redirect the Gateway returns 404 for "/my-path".
        fix: Add a rule that redirects the slashless path.
            - matches:
              - path:
                  type: Exact
                  value: "/my-path"
              filters:
              - type: RequestRedirect
                requestRedirect:
                  statusCode: 301
                  path:
                    type: ReplaceFullPath
                    replaceFullPath: "/my-path/"

LOW     NGX-NORM-001  Request paths are normalised before matching
        ingress-nginx normalises dot segments and repeated slashes before matching. How your Gateway
        implementation normalises paths cannot be determined from manifests; it has to be measured
        with requests.
